```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Different regulatory authorities weight the four R4SUB evidence pillars
(quality, trace, risk, usability) differently. The `r4subprofile` package
encodes these authority-specific requirements so that the SCI can be
calibrated accordingly.

```{r load}
library(r4subprofile)
```

## Supported authorities

```{r authorities}
list_authorities()
```

## Submission types per authority

```{r sub-types-fda}
list_submission_types("FDA")
list_submission_types("EMA")
```

## Creating a submission profile

`submission_profile()` returns a profile with authority-specific pillar
weights, decision bands, and required indicators:

```{r fda-nda}
fda_nda <- submission_profile("FDA", "NDA")
fda_nda$pillar_weights
fda_nda$minimum_coverage
```

```{r ema-maa}
ema_maa <- submission_profile("EMA", "MAA", study_phase = "Phase3")
ema_maa$pillar_weights
```

## Comparing authority weights

FDA NDA vs EMA MAA pillar weights:

```{r compare}
weights_df <- data.frame(
  pillar    = c("quality", "trace", "risk", "usability"),
  FDA_NDA   = unname(fda_nda$pillar_weights),
  EMA_MAA   = unname(ema_maa$pillar_weights)
)
weights_df
```

## Profile summary

`profile_summary()` prints a formatted summary of the profile and returns the
profile invisibly:

```{r profile-summary}
profile_summary(fda_nda)
```

Pass `format = "tibble"` to get the same information as a tidy, one-row-per-field
tibble that can be filtered, joined, or written out:

```{r profile-summary-tibble}
profile_summary(fda_nda, format = "tibble")
```

## Building your own profile

The shipped authorities cover the common filings, but a sponsor sometimes needs
to score against an internal gate, a regional ruleset, or guidance that is not
yet packaged. `custom_profile()` builds a profile from values you supply. Every
regulatory quantity is a required argument with no default, so the package
invents no weights or thresholds; you provide the numbers from your own
authoritative source, and the structure is validated the same way the built-in
profiles are (weights sum to 1, bands contiguous and covering their range):

```{r custom}
internal <- custom_profile(
  authority = "Internal",
  submission_type = "Gate2",
  pillar_weights = c(quality = 0.40, trace = 0.20, risk = 0.30, usability = 0.10),
  bands = list(
    ready = c(85, 100), minor_gaps = c(70, 84),
    conditional = c(50, 69), high_risk = c(0, 49)
  ),
  required_indicators = c("Q-MISS-VAR", "T-TRACE-LEVEL", "R-HIGH-RPN"),
  required_asset_types = c("dataset", "define"),
  minimum_coverage = 0.80,
  rpn_bands = list(
    critical = c(80, 125), high = c(40, 79),
    medium = c(15, 39), low = c(1, 14)
  ),
  default_detectability = 3L
)
internal
```

The result is an ordinary `submission_profile`, so it flows into every function
in the package, including `profile_sci_config()` and `validate_against_profile()`.

## Validating evidence against a profile

`validate_against_profile()` checks an evidence table against the
profile's required indicators and asset types:

```{r validate}
ev <- data.frame(
  run_id           = "run-001",
  study_id         = "STUDY01",
  asset_type       = c("dataset", "define", "program", "spec"),
  asset_id         = c("ADSL", "define.xml", "prod_adsl.R", "ADSL"),
  source_name      = "r4subcore",
  source_version   = "0.1.2",
  indicator_id     = c("Q-001", "Q-002", "R-001", "U-001"),
  indicator_name   = c("Quality Check", "Define Check",
                       "Program Validation", "Label Quality"),
  indicator_domain = c("quality", "quality", "risk", "usability"),
  severity         = "info",
  result           = "pass",
  metric_value     = 1,
  metric_unit      = "score",
  message          = "Check passed",
  location         = c("ADSL", "define.xml", "prod_adsl.R", "ADSL"),
  evidence_payload = "{}",
  created_at       = Sys.time(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

val <- validate_against_profile(ev, fda_nda)
val$is_compliant
val$coverage
val$missing_indicators
```

The `details` tibble shows per-requirement status:

```{r details}
head(val$details)
```

## Study phase

Some authorities adjust requirements based on study phase. Pass
`study_phase` to reflect phase-specific requirements:

```{r phase}
pmda_nda_p3 <- submission_profile("PMDA", "NDA_JP", study_phase = "Phase3")
pmda_nda_p3$pillar_weights
```

## Versioned rule packs

A profile answers "what does this authority require". A rule pack pins that to a
named, dated version, so a score can be reproduced and compared over time as
guidance changes. `rule_packs()` lists what is available:

```{r packs}
library(r4subprofile)
rule_packs()
```

Select one by id. Each indicator carries a `source` field for its authoritative
citation:

```{r pack}
pack <- rule_pack("fda-2026.1")
pack
head(rule_pack_indicators(pack))
```

The built-in packs ship with `source` set to `NA`: the citations are left for
entry from a controlled regulatory reference list, rather than filled with
unverified section numbers. Supply them when you have them:

```{r sources}
pack <- rule_pack(
  "fda-2026.1",
  sources = c("Q-MISS-VAR" = "FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide")
)
subset(rule_pack_indicators(pack), !is.na(source))
```

Record the pack on a scored result so the score can always be traced back to the
exact ruleset and version that produced it:

```{r provenance}
rule_pack_provenance(pack)
```
